subject.title: refactor(channels): move inbound turn execution into core

question: Should the shipped reply-dispatcher `onError` callback remain fire-and-forget while core receives a separate awaited cleanup hook, or is blocking dispatcher idle on arbitrary plugin callback completion an intentional compatibility change?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes callback completion timing across the shared channel lifecycle, and repository policy treats Plugin SDK behavior changes as compatibility-sensitive even when TypeScript declarations are unchanged.

options.title: Preserve observer semantics
options.body: Keep public `onError` non-blocking and introduce a separate internal awaited cleanup callback for channel-owned teardown.

options.title: Adopt awaited semantics
options.body: Accept the compatibility change only with explicit maintainer approval, bounded-stall behavior, upgrade documentation, and live plugin proof.

options.title: Split the timing change
options.body: Land the data-only core lifecycle separately and defer callback timing changes to a focused compatibility-reviewed PR.

recommendation.title: Preserve observer semantics
recommendation.body: Keep public `onError` non-blocking and introduce a separate internal awaited cleanup callback for channel-owned teardown.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the merged centralized lifecycle and authored the follow-up callback-timing implementation, making them the clearest owner of the intended contract.
